events.title: Server Move - Continued Progress
events.description: Omniscient continued the HF backend overhaul, working through the harder portions of the migration. The thread provides ongoing insight into the back-end work.

events.title: Awards
events.description: King Decade awarded to JX⠀, Nima304, and Riddick. Green Apple awarded to 6. Dicey awarded to Au Jus Demon.

events.title: Group & Crew Changes
events.description: 7 rebranded the Casino group into a new AI creative group called Vibe.

events.title: GFX Image of the Week
events.description: Motusora's GFX work was featured as the HF News image of the week.

events.title: Every AI chat assistant is now an ad company?
events.description: Hackers raised the uncomfortable point that an assistant shaping what you read, buy, and believe becomes one of the most valuable ad surfaces ever — sparking discussion of inevitability, the 'if it's free, you're the product' line, and oversharing with AI like therapy.

events.title: If WW3 started tomorrow, what would actually pump?
events.description: KyO posed a 'markets under stress' question that drew a chaotic mix of dark humor and practical takes covering raw materials, defense names, and prepper essentials.

events.title: How did you find HackForums?
events.description: R5N3T's lounge prompt spun into a mini oral history of HF — friends inviting friends, members searching 'hacking forums' back in the day, and the classic pipeline from game hacks/drama into IT, infosec, and community.

events.title: Small Things That Can Actually Make You Happy
events.description: R5N3T pulled together warm responses on small daily wins — nostalgia hits, tiny surprises, affectionate moments, and even random animals approaching on night walks.

events.title: So....Basically....
events.description: Omniscient explored language quirks ('so', 'basically', 'irregardless', starting with 'I') as a window into how people think and self-edit — with AI as the mirror, sparking debate over whether LLMs really 'learn you'.

events.title: Movie of the Week — Dead Man's Wire
events.description: Charlie Sheen submitted Dead Man's Wire as Movie of the Week, citing the production quality and the deeper detail that the film captured from the underlying story.
